title: First Morning Lecture
narrative: Your alarm goes off at 7:30 AM. The first real lecture of the semester starts in forty minutes, and your bed suddenly feels like the safest place on Earth.

choices.outcome: You arrive slightly sleepy but on time. The lecturer explains how the module works, and you feel like you actually know what's happening.
You wake up two hours later with three unread messages and a vague sense of academic guilt.

title: Messy Room
narrative: Your room looks like a crime scene. Clothes everywhere, empty cups forming a small civilization on your desk, and something in the bin that should have been taken out days ago.

choices.outcome: It takes an hour, but your space transforms. You can see the desk again. Your mental clarity improves almost immediately.
You navigate the obstacle course that is your floor and carry on. It's fine. Everything is fine. The smell will go away on its own. Probably.

title: Textbook Dilemma
narrative: The lecturer recommends an expensive textbook. The library has only two copies, both already taken. Your bank account looks nervous.

choices.outcome: Your wallet suffers, but you now have access to all the recommended material.
You find some decent notes online. They are not perfect, but they get the job done for now.
Future you will deal with it. Future you is already tired.

title: First Campus Party
narrative: A classmate invites you to a campus party. You barely know anyone, but everyone says this is how friendships start.

choices.outcome: You meet new people, laugh more than expected, and return home late but socially recharged.
You sleep early and wake up feeling human. Your social life, however, remains a loading screen.

title: Cheap Groceries
narrative: You are at the supermarket deciding between actual nutritious food and the legendary student combo: noodles, instant coffee, and biscuits.

choices.outcome: It costs more, but your body thanks you. You even feel like a responsible adult for approximately twelve minutes.
Financially efficient. Nutritionally questionable. Your dinner has the emotional depth of cardboard.
The food arrives fast and delicious. Your budget cries silently in the corner.

title: Study Group Invite
narrative: Some classmates are forming a study group. They seem motivated, organized, and slightly intimidating.

choices.outcome: The session is useful and you finally understand a topic that looked like ancient magic yesterday.
You make progress at your own pace, although you occasionally explain concepts to your desk lamp.
A peaceful evening. Academically dangerous, but peaceful.

title: Part-Time Job Offer
narrative: A local café is hiring students for evening shifts. The money would help, but your schedule is already starting to look cursed.

choices.outcome: You secure extra income, but your free time immediately disappears into the void.
You find a compromise. It is not perfect, but at least your calendar does not scream.
You protect your time and energy, but your bank account remains suspiciously quiet.

title: Forgotten Assignment
narrative: You open the course platform and discover an assignment due tonight. You have no memory of this task existing.

choices.outcome: It is not your best work, but it exists. Sometimes existence is enough.
The lecturer grants you two extra days. You feel both relieved and mildly ashamed.
Bold strategy. The gradebook will remember this.

title: Roommate Noise
narrative: Your roommate decides that midnight is the perfect time to reorganize furniture, cook loudly, and discover a new playlist.

choices.outcome: The conversation is awkward but productive. They apologize and promise to be quieter.
You stare at the ceiling while someone aggressively opens cupboards in the kitchen.
The message is technically polite, but the vibes are radioactive.

title: Library or Café?
narrative: You planned to study, but a friend suggests working together at a café. The library is free and quiet. The café has cake.

choices.outcome: You focus well and get through your notes. The silence is powerful, almost suspicious.
You study a little, chat a lot, and accidentally buy a pastry called 'academic motivation'.
You technically study, but your bed keeps trying to recruit you.

title: Student Club Fair
narrative: The campus is full of stands, flyers, free pens, and students passionately explaining hobbies you did not know existed.

choices.outcome: You sign up for one activity and meet people outside your course. Your week just became busier, but also more interesting.
You escape with three pens, a tote bag, and no new commitments.
You take the long route around campus. Peaceful, but a little isolating.

title: Midterm Revision
narrative: Midterms are approaching. Your notes are scattered across notebooks, slides, screenshots, and one mysterious document named 'final_final_real_notes.docx'.

choices.outcome: You organize everything into a realistic plan. For once, chaos fears you.
You study intensely but inefficiently. Some knowledge enters your brain. Some simply waves goodbye.
There is technically still time. There is also technically a storm approaching.

title: Extra Shift Request
narrative: Your manager asks if you can cover an extra shift this week. You could use the money, but you had planned to catch up on coursework.

choices.outcome: The money helps, but you leave work exhausted and with unread lecture notes staring at you.
You protect your study time. Your manager understands, although your wallet does not.

choices.text: Ask to do a shorter shift
choices.outcome: You compromise and survive the week with only moderate emotional damage.

title: Group Project Roles
narrative: Your group project begins. Everyone agrees to divide the work equally, which is usually student code for 'someone will suffer later'.

choices.outcome: You organize the team and set deadlines. It is stressful, but the project finally has direction.
You complete your section and hope everyone else does the same. Hope is not a project management tool, but here we are.
Nobody asks much of you. Unfortunately, nobody trusts you much either.

title: Friend Needs Help
narrative: A friend messages you saying they are overwhelmed and need someone to talk to. You were about to study.

choices.outcome: You lose study time, but your friend clearly needed support. The conversation matters.
It is not as meaningful as meeting in person, but it still helps.
You focus on your work, but the unread message sits there like a tiny emotional debt.

title: Unexpected Bill
narrative: An unexpected bill appears. It is not huge, but it is exactly large enough to ruin your weekly budget.

choices.outcome: Painful but responsible. Your finances take a hit, but the problem is gone.
You buy yourself some time, but the stress follows you around like a small angry cloud.

choices.text: Ask someone to split the cost
choices.outcome: After an awkward conversation, someone agrees to help cover part of it.

title: Presentation Prep
narrative: A presentation is coming up. The slides technically exist, but several of them are just titles and a stock photo of people pointing at a graph.

choices.outcome: You practice, fix weak slides, and feel almost professional.
You rely on charisma, caffeine, and the hope that nobody asks questions.
The group actually contributes. A rare academic miracle.

title: Rainy Commute
narrative: It is raining heavily. You have class soon, and the bus is late. The universe is testing your commitment to education.

choices.outcome: You arrive wet, cold, and academically present. A heroic but damp victory.
You miss the live discussion but catch up with recordings and notes.
You arrive on time and dry. Your budget, however, has been personally attacked.

title: Mental Health Day
narrative: You wake up exhausted in a way sleep does not fully explain. The day ahead feels heavier than usual.

choices.outcome: You cancel non-essential plans, rest, and feel more stable by evening.
You get things done, but it feels like running a laptop at 2 percent battery.
Opening up is uncomfortable, but it helps. You feel less alone.

title: Midterm Results
narrative: Midterm results are published. Your classmates are reacting with celebration, panic, or suspicious silence.

choices.outcome: You identify what went wrong and make a plan to improve. Painful, but useful.
You learn very little academically, but become an expert in unnecessary stress.
Regardless of the mark, you made it through. That deserves something small.

title: Family Call
narrative: Your family calls to ask how university is going. They mean well, but every question sounds like a performance review.

choices.outcome: You admit things have been difficult. The conversation is emotional, but supportive.
You keep the call short and cheerful. Afterwards, you feel strangely alone.
They help, but not without a long discussion about responsibility.

title: Group Conflict
narrative: Two members of your group project start arguing in the chat. The deadline is close, and the document is still unfinished.

choices.outcome: You calm things down and get everyone moving again, though it costs you patience you did not know you had.
The project improves, but resentment quietly moves into your soul.
They do not sort it out. Shocking development.

title: Career Talk
narrative: There is a career talk on campus. It sounds useful, but also like one of those events where everyone pretends to have a five-year plan.

choices.outcome: You learn about internships and leave with slightly more direction than before.
You make academic progress, but miss a chance to think about life after exams.

choices.text: Go only for the free snacks
choices.outcome: You eat three pastries and accidentally learn something about employability.

title: Final Project Deadline
narrative: The final project deadline is approaching. The file names in your folder suggest a tragic history of panic revisions.

choices.outcome: You work steadily and submit something you are genuinely proud of.
The project gets submitted, powered by caffeine, fear, and questionable formatting.
It is complete enough to be accepted, but not good enough to make you relax.

title: Friendship Drift
narrative: You realize you have barely spoken to some friends in weeks. Everyone is busy, but the distance is starting to feel real.

choices.outcome: Not everyone can come, but the ones who do remind you that connection still matters.
A few conversations restart. Small effort, meaningful result.
You promise yourself you will reconnect later. Later keeps getting heavier.

title: Final Exam Revision
narrative: Final exams are close. Your notes are better than they were at midterms, but the pressure feels much heavier now.

choices.outcome: You study consistently and still manage to sleep. A rare and elegant strategy.
You cover a lot of material, but your brain starts buffering during basic tasks.
Efficient, risky, and very much based on vibes.
You rest, but tomorrow's version of you is already preparing a complaint.

title: Exam Morning
narrative: It is the morning of an important exam. Your stomach is doing gymnastics and your brain is replaying random facts from unrelated modules.

choices.outcome: You feel nervous but prepared. At least your body is not running exclusively on panic.
You remember one extra concept and forget how breathing works.
You make it, but the stress of nearly being late follows you into the exam hall.

title: Internship Application
narrative: An internship application deadline appears. It could be great for your future, but your semester is already overloaded.

choices.outcome: You spend time improving your CV and writing a decent application. Future you may be grateful.
It is submitted, but the cover letter has the emotional range of a receipt.
You avoid extra stress now, but lose a possible opportunity.

title: End-of-Semester Party
narrative: Exams are almost over, and everyone is talking about one final party. You are tired, broke, and tempted.

choices.outcome: The night is memorable, even if some details are reconstructed from photos and group chat evidence.
You celebrate without completely destroying tomorrow. Mature? Perhaps.
You miss the fun, but your body sends a thank-you note.

title: Semester Reflection
narrative: The semester is nearly finished. You look back at the choices, compromises, disasters, and tiny victories that got you here.

choices.outcome: You recognize both mistakes and growth. It was messy, but you learned more than grades can show.

choices.text: Focus only on what went wrong
choices.outcome: You spiral through every bad decision. Reflection becomes self-roasting with extra steps.
You may not have mastered student life, but you made it through the semester. That counts.

title: Card Declined
narrative: You're at the grocery store checkout with a basket of essentials. Your card gets declined. The person behind you in line is watching. Your phone shows a balance of £0.43.

choices.outcome: It's a humbling phone call. They transfer some money but the lecture about budgeting lasts twenty minutes. You can practically hear the disappointment.
You awkwardly hand the basket back to the cashier and walk out with nothing. Dinner tonight is whatever's left in the cupboard. Ketchup packets it is.

title: Burnout Warning
narrative: You sit down to work, but the words blur together. Your body feels heavy, your patience is gone, and even simple tasks feel impossible.

choices.outcome: You step back before things get worse. The work waits, but you finally breathe.
You force yourself through the day, but your mind feels like a browser with forty tabs open and no memory left.
You contact someone and admit you are struggling. It does not fix everything, but it stops the spiral.

title: Academic Warning
narrative: An email from your lecturer appears with the subject line: 'Concern about your progress'. Your soul briefly leaves your body.

choices.outcome: The meeting is uncomfortable but useful. You finally understand what needs to improve.
You build a strict plan and commit to catching up. It will not be easy, but it is possible.
You close the email and pretend reality has been postponed. It has not.

title: Isolation Spiral
narrative: You notice that nobody has messaged you in days. Or maybe they did, and you were too tired to reply. Either way, the silence feels loud.

choices.outcome: The conversation starts awkwardly, but soon feels familiar. You remember you are not as alone as you thought.
It takes effort to show up, but being around people helps more than expected.
You avoid discomfort, but the room feels smaller by the hour.

title: Treat Yourself?
narrative: For once, your finances look stable. A dangerous thought appears: maybe you deserve something nice.

choices.outcome: You invest in something that genuinely improves your routine. Responsible luxury achieved.
You spend more than planned, but the night gives you stories worth keeping.
You resist temptation and keep your safety net intact. Slightly boring, extremely smart.

title: Scholarship Opportunity
narrative: Your strong academic performance makes you eligible for a small scholarship application. The deadline is soon.

choices.outcome: You prepare a strong application. Your effort might pay off beyond grades.
You send something acceptable, though not amazing. Still, an opportunity taken is better than one ignored.
You avoid extra work, but the opportunity passes quietly.

title: Support Network
narrative: Because you have stayed connected, your friends notice when you seem stressed. One of them offers to help before you even ask.

choices.outcome: You let someone support you. The week feels lighter, and the friendship feels stronger.

choices.text: Thank them but handle it alone
choices.outcome: You appreciate the offer, but keep carrying everything yourself. Admirable, but tiring.

title: A Surprisingly Good Routine
narrative: Somehow, against all odds, your routine is working. You are sleeping enough, eating decently, and not completely falling apart.

choices.outcome: You keep the balance going. It is not exciting, but stability is quietly powerful.

choices.text: Use the energy to study harder
choices.outcome: You push your advantage academically, but the balance starts to wobble.
You reconnect with people and enjoy yourself without completely losing control.
